subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which core policy shape is approved?
rationale: The request changes browser egress security semantics and public config/UX surface, while current code has only static allow/deny policy with hostname exceptions.

options.title: Design staged browser SSRF policy
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking, then evaluate interactive confirmation after the boundary is tested.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to a user-approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, redirect, and audit semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation starts.

options.title: Keep current static policy
options.body: Keep strict default plus hostname exceptions and document broad private-network browser access as an explicit trusted-environment opt-in.

recommendation.title: Design staged browser SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata blocking, then evaluate interactive confirmation after the boundary is tested.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible history across browser SSRF defaults, docs, and shared policy hardening.
